payload.title: Notice of Intended Marriage Explained Step by Step
payload.excerpt: A Notice of Intended Marriage, or NOIM, is the written notice every couple marrying in Australia gives to their authorised marriage celebrant before the wedding.
key_takeaways: The NOIM is the written notice section 42 of the Marriage Act 1961 requires, and you give it to the authorised celebrant who will marry you.
It must reach your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before your wedding.
Since 12 June 2024 it can be witnessed in person or by audio-visual link, though not online if you sign overseas.
Marry legally in Australia and celebrate abroad, and you need a NOIM; marry legally abroad, and you follow that country's rules instead.

faq.q: How long does a Notice of Intended Marriage last?
faq.a: As at November 2026, your NOIM must be with your celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before your wedding date. If your date moves, ask your celebrant whether your NOIM still stands.
It depends where you sign, and the full list is on the form, so ask your celebrant if you are unsure.

faq.q: Can we lodge a NOIM if we live overseas?
faq.a: Yes, if you plan to marry in Australia, with an in-person witness who is also overseas and is not a celebrant.

faq.q: Can we get married with less than one month's notice?
faq.a: Talk to your celebrant: you may be able to marry if a prescribed authority approves it, on grounds such as employment or travel commitments, celebration arrangements, medical reasons, legal proceedings or an error in giving notice.

faq.q: Do we need a NOIM if we are getting married overseas?
faq.a: No. The NOIM is for marriages solemnised in Australia by an authorised celebrant, and Australian celebrants cannot perform overseas marriages. Abroad, the local rules apply, and some countries ask for a Certificate of No Impediment.

faq.q: Can we change celebrants after lodging our NOIM?
faq.a: Yes. A NOIM can be transferred to another authorised celebrant, including at the couple's request.
